Hi Karthik,

We're seeing ~47 sellers in our October payout batch with VAT IDs that failed the validation step in your portal (failure codes attached). Payments to those sellers are currently in a pending state on our side — finance won't remit until we have a clear remediation path.

Can Redwood confirm whether the failures are:
- checksum / formatting errors, or
- cross-border residency mismatch (i.e., vendor marked as EU B2B but VAT record shows consumer), or
- known false positives from VIES timing?

We also need a recommendation for what to show on our invoice copy to those sellers if a reverse-charge or withholding determination is required. If possible, a short template for a seller attestation (ownership of VAT, place-of-supply statement) would help speed up collection.

Attaching the failure export: vat_lookup_fails.csv

Thanks — wanting to close the payout window by Friday.

— Alyssa

Ben / Soojin — need your signoff on the conditional remit and the precise wording for the invoice memo (reverse-charge vs withholding). Marissa — can ops run the VIES+provider re-check and return a deduped list by EOD?

Agree with the approach in principle. A couple of finance constraints:
- We cannot leave funds indefinitely pending attestation — propose 30 calendar days hold, after which we either: remit with a gross-up and notify NovaLens, or initiate a longer escalation (invoice correction).
- Need a clear ledger entry: mark line-items as 'provisional hold — VAT validation' and capture the withholding reason code.

Soojin — legal input needed on whether the attestation alone is sufficient to treat these as B2B reverse-charge (I suspect not for residency disputes). If not, we should require evidence of business registration (VAT certificate) and a signed attestation declaring place-of-supply.

Marissa — run the batch recheck and produce: (a) clean failures list, (b) proposed 30-day hold roster with amounts, (c) messaging copy for sellers. Include a column 'recommended action' (attest / request docs / escalate).

Subject: Re: Seller VAT check — legal view and attestation requirements

Ben / Karthik — quick legal POV:

- Attestation by itself is borderline for residency disputes. For reverse-charge to apply safely, we want either a valid EU VAT number (VIES match) or two pieces of corroborating evidence (company registration excerpt + bank statement or VAT certificate).
- For sellers who are non-EU or consumers, NovaLens should treat payments as subject to local withholding (if applicable) and issue invoices accordingly.
- Template attestation is fine as an initial triage step. Use it to triage sellers into: (A) immediate release if VIES validated, (B) request docs for residency, (C) escalate for tax counsel.

I've reviewed the template (attached) and added a clause requesting a scanned VAT certificate or a government registration snippet if the seller lands in category B. Also recommend a short privacy/data line: 'documents submitted for tax validation will be retained for 6 months and used solely to verify tax status.'

Cc: Erik Lund from Euratax — if you can confirm whether a signed attestation + VAT cert historically suffices for your clients, would appreciate it.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Seller VAT check — operational plan and next steps

Alyssa / team — we've run the VIES + provider re-check against the attached export. Summary: 47 initial failures -> 22 auto-resolved (format / cache hits) -> 25 remaining (19 residency mismatches, 6 checksum failures that need manual seller confirmation).

Actionable plan (we'll execute today):
1) Send the attached seller attestation template to the 25 sellers (email copy below). Sellers will have 7 calendar days to upload docs to NovaLens's secure intake form.
2) Place a 30-day provisional hold on the 25 payout line-items; mark ledger entries as 'provisional hold — VAT validation (reason code: RV-MISMATCH)'. Platform fees will be remitted as requested.
3) If seller provides VAT cert + attestation within 7 days, we clear and remit within the next payout cycle. If not, escalate to tax counsel (Erik copied) for collection/withhold guidance.
4) We'll publish a short invoice memo template you can include: 'Payment subject to VAT validation. If VAT ID invalid, tax treatment may change; please provide VAT documentation within 7 days to avoid hold.'

Email copy to sellers (short):
---
Subject: Action required to release your NovaLens payout
Hi {SellerName},
We attempted to validate your VAT ID but the record could not be verified. To avoid a hold on your payout, please complete the attached attestation and upload a VAT certificate or business registration document within 7 days: {secure intake link}.
If we do not receive documents within 7 days, your payout will be placed on a provisional hold for up to 30 days while we escalate for tax review.
Thanks,
NovaLens Payments Team
---

I've attached the CSV with the final 25 rows: vat_lookup_fails.csv (cleaned) and the attestation template. Let us know if you want Redwood to host attestation intake (we can offer a lightweight intake form + secure upload).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
